html:
The Gambia became independent from Britain on 18 February 1965, with Dawda Jawara as prime minister. In 1970 it became a republic and he became president.

Many in London and Senegal doubted that a strip of land along a river, with a few hundred thousand people and groundnuts as its main export, could survive alone, and a union with Senegal was discussed. The Gambia stayed separate, kept English and its own currency, and for almost thirty years held regular multiparty elections, rare in West Africa then. The ties with Senegal led later to the Senegambia Confederation.
sum: The Gambia became independent from Britain on 18 February 1965, with Dawda Jawara as prime minister. In 1970 it became a republic and he became president.
